name: Belmar Groves Apartments
headline: Metro West Housing Solutions (Lakewood's housing authority) completed a $66.5 million renovation of Belmar Groves, 118 existing one- to three-bedroom apartments at 259 S Teller St near Lakewood's Belmar district, financed with a 2023-cycle federal 4% credit and $30 million of its own tax-exempt bonds.
why_it_matters: A housing-authority-issued bond and 4% resyndication that layered Division of Housing, Jefferson County, EPA brownfields money and city fee waivers to fully rehab an aging tax credit property in a high-cost location and deepen affordability to 50% AMI for 63 units.

status.label: Renovation completed (October 2025)
status.detail: Jefferson County reported that construction began in August 2023 and the renovation was completed in October 2025. The deal is still on CHFA's 4% award report as of 2026-09-21, which means 8609 forms had not yet been issued.

next_step: Watch for the deal to move to CHFA's 4% Completed Developments Report (8609 issuance).

key_numbers.meaning: 36 one-, 70 two- and 12 three-bedroom units in 10 buildings; CHFA lists all 118 at 60% AMI, while the county says 63 are now at 50% AMI or below.
Federal credit runs 10 years; the county reports $22.6M of tax credit equity. Amounts on CHFA's report are marked subject to change.

key_numbers.value: $30,000,000 in tax-exempt bonds issued by Metro West Housing Solutions
key_numbers.meaning: The housing authority is its own bond issuer; whose bond cap was used is not stated publicly.
Total project cost reported by Jefferson County at completion.

facts.value: Family, acquisition/rehabilitation; not in a QCT, DDA or SADDA; Section 8 column marked No
One block from the Belmar shopping district
Listed as a 4% tax credit and tax-exempt bond property placed in service in 2006 with 117 of 118 units low-income (listing site drawing on HUD LIHTC data)

All 118 units renovated with reconfigured open kitchen, dining and living areas, new cabinets, counters, appliances, flooring, lighting and plumbing fixtures; new siding, windows, roofs and entry doors, with mansard roofs removed; new high-efficiency heating and cooling; accessibility upgrades

Community building gutted and expanded by about 1,000 sq ft (lounge, computer lab, kitchenette); new 24-hour fitness room; rebuilt laundry, playground, community garden and barbecue areas; expanded green space
U.S. EPA provided $500,000; the renovation was supported by EPA grants per the housing authority (the grant's specific purpose is not stated in these sources)

money.note: Cycle year 2023; about $22.6M of tax credit equity per Jefferson County.

money.source: Tax-exempt private activity bonds (Metro West Housing Solutions)
money.note: Whose bond cap is not stated publicly.
Form (grant or loan) not stated in the county release; the housing authority describes Division of Housing grants.

parties.role: Sponsor (as CHFA prints it), owner and bond issuer
parties.name: Metro West Housing Solutions (Housing Authority of the City of Lakewood)
Colorado Division of Housing; Jefferson County; U.S. EPA; City of Lakewood (fee waivers)

background.text: Metro West Housing Solutions already controlled Belmar Groves, one of its 18 communities; the acquisition/rehabilitation label reflects a transfer into a new tax credit ownership (inferred), and no third-party sale or price was found in public records.
Jefferson County described the property as not significantly updated in decades before the work, which began in August 2023.

By August 2024, 32 of 118 units were fully renovated and exterior work on three buildings was complete; the housing authority then expected completion in early 2025. The county reported completion in October 2025.
Before the renovation all units were restricted at 60% AMI; afterward 63 units are affordable at 50% AMI or below, per the county.
The deal does not appear in CHFA's 2023 Round One or Round Two applicant reports or the 2023 Round Two award report.

Purpose of the EPA grant (brownfields cleanup or other) and the form of the Division of Housing funds (a State Housing Board award of about $3.54M is indexed on DOLA's site, but the page returned an error and could not be verified).
